question_text: Kapil invested 2000 rupees in a bank account on January 1st 2012. The account pays 8.25% per annum compounded annually.

subparts.stem: Find the total value of Kapil's investment on January 1st 2019.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up compound interest formula with n = 7 and i = 0.0825
Obtaining approximately 3483.58 and rounding to 3484 rupees

subparts.solution: The interest is calculated annually, so $n = 7$ time periods. $u_7 = u_0 \times (1 + i)^7 = 2000 \times (1.0825)^7 \approx 3483.58$. The total value of Kapil's investment on January 1st 2019 is $3484\text{ rupees}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Compound interest compounded annually follows $u_n = u_0(1 + i)^n$, where $i$ is the annual interest rate as a decimal.
step_by_step: Round to the nearest whole rupee: 3484 rupees.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Incorrect conversion of percentage to decimal (e.g., using $0.825$ instead of $0.0825$).

subparts.stem: Would it have been a better option for Kapil to invest his money in an account paying 8% per annum interest compounded monthly? Justify your answer.

mark_breakdown.desc: Calculating number of periods n = 84 and periodic interest rate
Calculating the future value to be approx 3494.84 (or 3495 rupees)
Concluding that the monthly compounding option is better by 11 rupees

subparts.solution: There are $n = 7 \times 12 = 84$ time periods. Each time period the investment increases by $i = \frac{8\%}{12} \approx 0.667\%$. The value after 7 years is $u_{84} = u_0 \times (1 + i)^{84} \approx 2000 \times (1.00667)^{84} \approx 3494.84$. The total value of Kapil's investment on January 1st 2019 for this account is $3495\text{ rupees}$, which is 11 rupees more than the account in a. Therefore, investing in the account paying $8\%$ per annum interest compounded monthly is the better option.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: For monthly compounding, multiply the number of years by 12 to get periods $n$, and divide the annual rate by 12 to get the periodic interest rate $i$.
step_by_step: Compute compound value: $2000 \times (1 + \frac{0.08}{12})^{84} \approx 3494.84$, rounding to $3495\text{ rupees}$.
Compare with part a: $3495 - 3484 = 11\text{ rupees}$ more, making monthly compounding better.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Rounding the monthly rate prematurely, which can lead to significant discrepancies over 84 periods.
